as_written_in_papers.quote: Genetic testing confirmed the diagnosis of Danon disease with a LAMP2 c.733C > T (p.G245*) mutation (Figure 1M).

cases.statement: One person: a 25-year-old woman (single case report). Zygosity is not stated in the text; she is female, so she would carry one copy on one X, but the paper does not say heterozygous.

people.label: patient (A 25-year-old woman)
people.key_phenotypes: cardiac hypertrophy and Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome; hypertrophic non-obstructive cardiomyopathy (septum 19 mm) progressing to enlarged heart with reduced biventricular systolic function (LVEF 27%, RVEF 15%); atrial fibrillation, non-sustained ventricular tachycardia; extensive late gadolinium enhancement; heart transplantation

quotes.quote: A 25-year-old woman with cardiac hypertrophy and Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome sought diagnosis and treatment at our hospital.
the echocardiogram revealed hypertrophic non-obstructive cardiomyopathy, with a maximum ventricular septum thickness of 19 mm (Figure 1B) 6 years ago.
Both electrocardiogram and Holter monitoring identified atrial fibrillation, frequent ventricular premature beats (9261 beats/24 h), and non-sustained ventricular tachycardia.
The left and right ventricular ejection fractions were markedly reduced to 27% and 15%, respectively
The patient ultimately underwent a heart transplantation and was in good condition at the 3-month follow-up.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Cardiac features (hypertrophy, pre-excitation, later dilated phase) are described by the authors as consistent with Danon disease; exclusion of other causes (other genes, panel scope) is not reported.

quotes.quote: These findings led to the consideration of a decompensation phase in inherited metabolic cardiomyopathy.
Danon disease, a rare X-linked dominant lysosomal disorder, predominantly manifests as myocardial hypertrophy, though some patients, particularly females, may develop a dilated phenotype.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: From the batch HGVS, c.733C>T is a nonsense change predicted p.(Gln245Ter). The paper states no mechanism.

authors_classification.statement: No classification stated; authors say testing 'confirmed the diagnosis' with this 'mutation'.

quotes.quote: Genetic testing confirmed the diagnosis of Danon disease with a LAMP2 c.733C > T (p.G245*) mutation (Figure 1M).

concerns: Protein mismatch: the paper writes p.G245* but c.733C>T on NM_002294.3 predicts p.(Gln245Ter) (Q245*); 'G' may be a typo for Gln, or the cDNA could be wrong. The paper gives no transcript, and the genetic result is shown only in Figure 1M (not in the text).
Very short image-type case report (European Heart Journal Case Reports): no zygosity, family history, parental testing or testing method stated.
notes_for_panel: Single female case; the only variant evidence is one sentence plus Figure 1M. The panel may wish to view Figure 1M to resolve the G245*/Q245* discrepancy.
